clues.text: Told to preach against Nineveh, Jonah went down to Joppa and paid his fare on a ship sailing here.
Angry that Nineveh was spared, Jonah told God he fled here because he knew God was gracious and would relent.
King Solomon's ships named for this place arrived every three years with gold, ivory, apes, and peacocks.
Jehoshaphat joined wicked King Ahaziah to build ships at Ezion-geber to sail here, but they were wrecked.
Ezekiel says this place traded silver, iron, tin, and lead for the wares of Tyre.
Jeremiah mocks idols covered with hammered silver brought from here and gold from Uphaz.
A psalm for the king prays that the kings of this place and distant shores will bring tribute.
